The largest hydroelectric power station.why: People say that the Three Gorges Dam is the largest hydroelectric power station in the world and that it stands on the Yangtze, each readily and thousands of times. Nobody ranks the power stations of a single river when the first of them is the world's biggest: 'the largest hydroelectric power station on the Yangtze' is not the kind of thing anyone writes. All three wordings have no exact hit, against 376 for the world-wide premise and 1,976 for the dam on the Yangtze. Wikipedia's Yangtze article does join the two in one sentence, so a model may have seen it, but it follows from the two premises every model holds.

notes: Derived edit (premises about individuals only: the Three Gorges Dam is the largest station in the world, it stands on the Yangtze, plus the rule that the world's largest is also the largest on its own river). Derivability very_likely: no exact form of the river-level fact occurs while both premises are stated hundreds to thousands of times; Wikipedia joins them in one sentence of the Yangtze article. The relations (staging, technology-replace-abox) are has_largest_hydro_station (functional, inverse largest_hydro_station_on) and stands_on_river (functional, chain with located_in). Related near is functional through stands_on_river: the edit puts the Hoover Dam on the Yangtze, and a dam stands on one river. The determinate derived queries: a premise-route binding (the longest river in China; a model that kept both premises answers the Three Gorges Dam), a subproperty question through Wuhan, and a composition question about the river's mouth. The worlds are lopsided in real capacity terms (the Hoover Dam is far smaller than the Three Gorges Dam, so w2 is the less natural world) and kept unweighted; as in the Honshu template, w1 keeps the original answer, so a model that never propagated the edit also matches w1: read it together with the direct and premise-route answers.
